messages:
Maya (AE): FYI opening thread for NordBank POC. security/compliance insists on EU-only processing, BYOK in customer account, and a signed attestation that no non-EU subprocessors touch request payloads. can we scope?
Raj (SE): hi all. two specific asks from their RFP: a minimal subprocessor roster for the EU path, and exact failover semantics if eu-west-1 is saturated (they want deterministic behavior).
Paolo (Infra): we can enforce an EU-only routing policy. options: strict pin to primary EU region (fail-hard), region pin with automatic EU failover (eu-west-2), or spill to an isolated dedicated EU pool. For BYOK, we proxy the KMS calls from our EU control plane to the customer's EU KMS endpoint.
Claire (Security): with BYOK we must capture and share KMS audit entries (key usage) and a KMS config checklist. signed attestation: security can produce a signed export stating data processed within EU regions and list of subprocessors involved. note: telemetry/monitoring vendors must be EU-hosted to appear on the EU-only subprocessor list.
Maya (AE): procurement wants a one-line exec summary + a formal attestation artifact. they also asked if packet captures are an option for validation during POC.
Paolo (Infra): packet capture is heavy and needs a support engagement; we can do pcap inside the customer's VPC (if private) or provide VPC flow logs and connection traces from our EU control plane. we can sign the exported logs with a timestamped signature.
Raj (SE): sample routing snippet for the POC (pseudo yaml):
```
redwood_routing:
  mode: "strict_eu"
  primary: "eu-west-1"
  failover:
    mode: "eu_only_regional"
    targets: ["eu-west-2"]
    behavior: "spill_to_dedicated_pool"
  kms: {mode: "byok", endpoint: "customer-kms-eu.example.com"}
```
Raj (SE): behavior "spill_to_dedicated_pool" will direct overflow to a reserved dedicated pool in EU (separate billing). otherwise we can queue requests but customer said they prefer no queuing.
Sam (Sales Ops): pricing question: if we provision a short-lived dedicated EU pool for the POC, procurement wants both an illustrative monthly commit and a pro-rated 2-week example. Paolo, any quick numbers?
Paolo (Infra): rough thumb: for sequential length ~256 tokens, average 20 QPS, peak 80 QPS, a 2-week dedicated node set (small) will likely be ~€7k-€12k pro-rated. Hosted burst would be token-priced; dedicated reserve clearly higher for short POC. I'll produce a precise sim once we confirm duty cycles.
Zoe (Legal): I'll draft a minimal EU subprocessor list (cloud provider EU regions, EU-based logging+monitoring vendor, internal support ops). if they require a clause banning any non-EU subprocessors, we should flag Private installation as an option (customer-owned infra).
Claire (Security): also note: if they want us to remove telemetry or obfuscate request-level metadata entirely, that pushes us toward Private deployment or a strict dedicated pipeline without external analytics.
Maya (AE): do we have ETA to produce the attestation + subprocessor list doc and the one-pager for their execs?
infra-bot: ticket NB-POC-19 created. infra provisioning ETA: 4 business days for EU route + BYOK test harness.
Paolo (Infra): I'll have a cost sim and POC provisioning checklist in 48 hours.
Raj (SE): I'll draft the one-pager and include failover flow diagrams + the test script: 1) validate BYOK handshake, 2) run steady 20 QPS for 2 hours, 3) spike to 80 QPS for 15m, 4) trigger failover and validate no payload leaves EU.
Sam (Sales Ops): I'll prepare a pro-forma commercial with hosted token example vs dedicated pro-rate and clause for additional inter-region egress charges if they opt for cross-AZ replication.
Zoe (Legal): I'll attach the subprocessor list and a recommended addendum for EU-only processing; flagging any telemetry partners that are currently global.
Claire (Security): timeline works. we'll also prepare the KMS audit export template (signed) and a checklist for their pen-test team.
Maya (AE): thanks team. scheduled sync in 36 hours to review artifacts. please add any blockers here before the sync. :wave:
